cases.title: Stair programming.
cases.note: Recorded route on a native-world cutaway. Step 35 runs first, followed by all three circuits of Step 36. Playback follows projected path length; it omits pauses and does not show real execution speed.

commands.text: mcapi press MOVE_FORWARD 1.3 && mcapi look --yaw 180 --pitch 15 --mode absolute && mcapi press MOVE_FORWARD 1.3 && mcapi look --yaw -90 --pitch 15 --mode absolute && mcapi press MOVE_FORWARD 1.3 && mcapi look --yaw 0 --pitch 15 --mode absolute && mcapi press MOVE_FORWARD 1.3 && mcapi look --yaw 90 --pitch 15 --mode absolute && mcapi state
commands.caption: One circuit · Y40 → Y48

commands.text: for i in 1 2 3; do for yaw in 90 180 -90 0; do mcapi look --yaw "$yaw" --pitch 15 --mode absolute; mcapi press MOVE_FORWARD 1.3; done; done; mcapi look --yaw 90 --pitch 15 --mode absolute; mcapi state
commands.caption: Three circuits · Y48 → Y56 → Y64 → Y72

cases.description: At Step 35, this sequence completes one circuit around the stairwell, raising the agent from Y40 to Y48. At Step 36, Astra uses a loop to repeat the four-heading movement pattern three times within one tool request, ascending through Y56 and Y64 to Y72.

title.text: Mine Odyssey: Benchmarking Spatial Agentic Intelligence in the Wild

hero-title.text: Benchmarking Spatial Agentic Intelligence in the Wild

hero-description.text: a benchmark for evaluating agentic spatial intelligence using Minecraft reconstructions of real-world locations.

overview-definition.text: Acquire and update spatial information through interaction, adapting actions as new evidence emerges.
overview-definition.source_text: the ability to proactively acquire and continually update spatial information through interaction, use it to guide observation and action, and adapt those actions as new evidence emerges
overview-definition.adaptation: Author-requested concise introduction; retains the manuscript meaning and omits the repeated task definition and detailed examples.

overview-task.text: Find routes and entrances, open doors, and move between levels.
overview-task.source_text: Each task provides a natural-language instruction specifying which waypoints to visit and in what order. Completing these tasks requires agents to find accessible routes and entrances, open doors, and move between levels using stairs and ladders, while monitoring their progress
overview-task.adaptation: Author-requested concise introduction; retains the manuscript meaning and omits the repeated task definition and detailed examples.

worlds.text: It comprises 180 tasks covering 30 such locations across 20 countries and regions on five continents, including 20 outdoor and 10 indoor settings.

terrain.text: These environments present diverse terrain and spatial constraints, including uneven ground, water boundaries, narrow corridors, and multilevel spaces.

interactions.text: Ascending stairs, climbing ladders, opening fence gates, or activating buttons to pass through doors.
interactions.source_text: ascending stairs, climbing ladders, opening fence gates, or activating buttons to pass through doors
interactions.adaptation: Sentence case and terminal period for excerpt.

task-definition.text: each task specifies a map, a starting waypoint and orientation, and an ordered sequence of destinations described in a natural-language instruction.

task-route.text: The agent must identify and visit these destinations in order, choosing its own route using the permitted controls and ending at the final waypoint.

task-position.text: Each waypoint pairs a human-readable place name with a three-dimensional arrival position in a specific Minecraft world.

task-order.text: Only the next required waypoint is eligible for credit; out-of-order visits do not advance task progress.

task-completion.text: After visiting all required destinations, the agent must submit an accepted claim_done to complete the task successfully.

system-intro.text: we develop a programmable control interface that combines API-based player control with keyboard and mouse input.

system-observation.text: The in-game map provides a top-down view of the explored environment and supports panning, zooming or searching to inspect different areas.

system-action.text: The agent uses these tools through Bash, either executing individual operations or composing multiple operations within a single Bash tool call with shell commands or Python scripts.

system-verifier.text: An independent evaluator is used to verify arrivals by comparing the player's position with the annotated waypoint coordinates. It samples the client player position at 1 Hz throughout execution, including during model inference.

results-intro.text: GPT-6 Astra leads at 85.6% SR, followed by Claude Opus 5.5 at 73.9%.

metric-sr.text: Fraction of tasks completed by visiting all required stops in order and submitting an accepted claim_done.
metric-sr.source_text: We evaluate each model on 180 tasks and report Success Rate (SR), the fraction of tasks where the agent visits all required stops in order and submits an accepted claim_done.
metric-sr.adaptation: Direct website definition, preserving the manuscript metric and scope.

metric-cc.text: Average fraction of ordered intermediate stops reached, measuring partial progress.
metric-cc.source_text: We also report Checkpoint Coverage (CC), the average fraction of ordered intermediate stops to measure partial progress.
metric-cc.adaptation: Direct website definition, preserving the manuscript metric and scope.

metric-spl.text: Successful completion weighted by route efficiency; shorter successful routes receive higher scores.
metric-spl.source_text: SPL measures efficiency by rewarding successful completion along shorter routes.
metric-spl.adaptation: Direct website definition, preserving the manuscript metric and scope.

metric-pl.text: Average full-episode 3D distance across all 180 tasks, including failures, sampled at approximately 1 Hz.
metric-pl.source_text: PL averages the full-episode 3D distance, computed from consecutive position samples at approximately 1 Hz, over all 180 tasks including failures.
metric-pl.adaptation: Direct website definition, preserving the manuscript metric and scope.

metric-turns.text: Average number of agent turns per task, excluding automatic history-summary responses.
metric-turns.source_text: Average turns is the average number of agent turns following the agent loop in Section and exclude automatic history-summary responses.
metric-turns.adaptation: Direct website definition, preserving the manuscript metric and scope.

results-caption.text: Main results on 180 tasks, with success rates broken down by 125 outdoor and 55 indoor tasks. SR, CC, and SPL are percentages; PL is the mean sampled 3D distance over all tasks.

recovery-intro.text: In both cases, Astra redirects its search and follows an alternative route to the target, while the unsuccessful models continues exploring within the same local region.

white-house-title.text: White House: Astra takes a detour; DeepSeek revisits rooms.

white-house-detail.text: DeepSeek recognizes the blocked passage but spent 142.7 minutes repeatedly revisiting the nearby rooms until the step limit. Astra instead inspects its surroundings, returns toward a southern doorway, and follows the hallway around the wall to Queen's Bedroom, completing the displayed detour in 2.4 minutes.

plaza-title.text: Plaza Hotel: Astra returns downstairs; Grok remains upstairs.

plaza-detail.text: Grok remains upstairs for 135.7 minutes before reaching the step limit. Astra instead retraces its route to the stairs, descends to the restaurant floor, and reaches the target in 12.6 minutes.

appendix-intro.text: Together, these cases show how agents use programming to turn visual map information into explicit coordinates and individual movement commands into reusable action sequences.
